facts.statement: The study used a rat model of traumatic brain injury created by controlled cortical impact, with animals receiving two one-hour inhalations of 4% hydrogen gas.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: In the injured rats, breathing hydrogen gas was associated with less swelling in the brain and fewer signs of neurological damage.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The treatment led to a higher count of M2-type microglia and a lower count of M1-type microglia in the brain tissue.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Exposure to hydrogen gas lowered the activity of the genes Jak2, Stat1, Stat3, and Hmgb1.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The authors suggest that the protective effect of hydrogen may work by blocking the JAK/STAT signaling pathway, which in turn changes how microglia cells behave.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue
